data.text: Prototypes can be classified as throwaway, incremental, or evolutionary. Throwaway prototypes are used for quick evaluation and are often created using fast and inexpensive low-fidelity mockups. Incremental prototypes involve testing separate modules before integration, while evolutionary prototypes involve refining a simple version of the entire system until it becomes the final product.
points: Prototypes can be classified as throwaway, incremental, or evolutionary.
Throwaway prototypes are used for quick evaluation and then discarded.
Low-fidelity mockups and paper sketches are suitable for throwaway prototypes because they are easy and inexpensive to create.
Incremental prototypes involve prototyping and testing separate modules before integrating them into the overall system.
Evolutionary prototypes involve refining a simple version of the whole system until it becomes the final product.

data.text: Expert evaluation is a quick and cost-effective way to assess a prototype at an early design stage. It requires a low-fidelity prototype and a team of three to five design team members or domain experts who provide feedback to save time and costs. Each evaluator independently produces a report, which is then combined into a final list of usability issues.
points: Quick evaluation is a fast and cheap way to assess a prototype at an early design stage.
The process requires at least a low-fidelity prototype and a team of evaluators.
Design team members or experts perform the evaluation because they are faster and cheaper to engage than end users, who may optionally be included.
A team of three to five members is sufficient for the evaluation.
Evaluators work independently to create reports that are then combined into a final list of usability issues.

data.text: Cognitive walkthrough is a quick expert evaluation technique used to identify usability problems by inspecting a prototype. The method requires a team of three to five members and at least a low-fidelity vertical prototype. Evaluators perform interface-level tasks from a scenario using predefined usability questions as guidelines. Finally, the evaluators provide detailed reports on their difficulties, which are then analyzed to identify broader usability issues.
points: Cognitive walkthrough is a quick expert evaluation technique used to identify usability problems by inspecting a prototype.
The method requires a team of three to five members and at least a low-fidelity vertical prototype.
Evaluators perform interface-level tasks from a scenario using predefined usability questions as guidelines.
Evaluators provide detailed reports on their difficulties, which are analyzed to identify broader usability issues.

data.text: Heuristic evaluation is a technique where evaluators use a checklist of heuristics to assess a prototype and perform a comprehensive evaluation without a task scenario. This process can use system-specific checklists or broader principles like Nielsen's 10 heuristics, which are applicable to most interactive systems. A team of at least three to five evaluators can use these heuristics to identify violations in low-fidelity prototypes and compile reports to highlight major issues.
points: Heuristic evaluation is a technique where evaluators assess a prototype using a checklist of heuristics without a task scenario.
Checklists for evaluating interfaces can be system-specific or focus on broader usability principles.
Nielsen's 10 heuristics are a general set applicable to most interactive systems.
Heuristic evaluation can be conducted on low-fidelity prototypes by a team of at least three to five evaluators.
Evaluators report whether each heuristic is followed or violated and compile these reports to identify major issues.
